rv.q: There’s bones of a solid play in “Shaw vs. Tunney.” Unfortunately, they’re without flesh.
Frankly, I came away from this play with the sense that it needlessly draws out the story of one summer on the Adriatic into a two-hour affair, with little substance for modern audiences to chew on.
Grippo Stage Company’s new World Premiere production is a knockout event in two acts.

The script for Shaw vs. Tunney, now on stage in a world premiere by Grippo Stage Company, delivers on all levels with sharp, insightful dialogue and insights into the personalities of the two principals: Legendary Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw and champion prizefighter Gene Tunney.
It just might be one of those “little engine that could” presentations that captures a growing audience for “SHAW vs. TUNNEY” during its world premiere run at Theater Wit.
Shaw vs. Tunney finally delivers as a keenly felt portrait of a seemingly unlikely friendship between two men.
I am certain there will be additional anecdotes that will be as enjoyable as the ones in this beyond-excellent production.
All-in-all it is a wonderful production.

cn.t: Critics find this world premiere about the unlikely friendship between George Bernard Shaw and boxer Gene Tunney fascinating in concept but unevenly executed, with strong performances elevating a script that some find static and dramatically inert.
